result_expr: Integral(rho*c*w(x)*Derivative(T(x, t), t), (x, 0, L)) + Integral(k(x)*Derivative(w(x), x)*Derivative(T(x, t), x), (x, 0, L)) - Integral(w(x)*Q(x), (x, 0, L)) - Subs(w(x)*k(x)*Derivative(T(x, t), x), x, L) + Subs(w(x)*k(x)*Derivative(T(x, t), x), x, 0)

steps.operation: move all terms to one side

steps.statement: Int_0^L rho c w dT/dt dx - Int_0^L w d/dx(k dT/dx) dx - Int_0^L w Q dx = 0  [W m^-2]
w d/dx(k dT/dx) = d/dx(w k dT/dx) - k dw/dx dT/dx
Int_0^L w d/dx(k dT/dx) dx = [w k dT/dx]_{x=L} - [w k dT/dx]_{x=0} - Int_0^L k dw/dx dT/dx dx; both boundary terms kept since w is not assumed zero at the ends
steps.operation: integrate S5 over (0, L) with the fundamental theorem of calculus (integration by parts)

steps.statement: R = Int_0^L rho c w dT/dt dx + Int_0^L k dw/dx dT/dx dx - Int_0^L w Q dx - [w k dT/dx]_{x=L} + [w k dT/dx]_{x=0} = 0; every term in W m^-2

assumptions_used: rho and c are constant (so they can stay inside or come out of the time-derivative integral)
T, w, k and Q are smooth on [0, L], so the product rule and the fundamental theorem of calculus apply
w is not assumed to vanish at x = 0 or x = L, so both boundary flux terms are kept
Sign convention: R is the integral of w*(rho c T_t - (k T_x)_x - Q), so the storage term is positive; -R is an equally valid residual
